limited_overlap.description: Applicants with prior earnings from 49,650 to 164,370 dollars: 225 training rows, 85% of them with estimated enrolment propensity outside 0.02-0.98. Enrolment was rare there, so the effects for these applicants rest on few enrolled rows and on model extrapolation. 14.5% of all training rows are outside the bounds.
Applicants who did not answer the follow-up survey: their earnings are not observed, and the estimates assume non-response depends only on the covariates and enrolment.

258 of 4000 new applicants have an estimated propensity outside (0.02, 0.98); their effects are extrapolations (flags in cate_overlap_flags.parquet).
The arm-specific aipw estimate is 2,336 dollars (90% interval 163 to 4,509). The reported ATE is the pooled augmented score; the arm-specific outcome models extrapolate in the high-prior stratum.

Intervals for the ATE, ATT, subgroups and the employment effect are normal intervals of the mean of the augmented scores over the chosen rows. They describe the sampled applicants and do not add variance for the nuisance models.
Earnings for non-respondents are missing. The estimates assume response is missing at random given the covariates and enrolment.
